model_meta.description: Concept-level representation of a miniature ball bearing assembly that permits shaft alignment through limited spherical movement of the bearing outer race while the inner race rotates.

subsystems.description: Retainer with conical inner bearing seat and outer mounting wall; supports the bearing and provides an installation interface.
Ball bearing with inner and outer races; the outer race has an arcuate, generally spherical outside wall and can pivot relative to the retainer.

interfaces.interface_type: Compression-ring force contact at outer race, permitting spherical movement with less resistance than rotational movement and thereby restraining outer-race rotation.

subsystems.description: Elastomeric ring applies force to the outer race, maintaining engagement with the bearing seat while accommodating spherical motion and resisting outer-race rotation.
External shaft received through the inner race and rotated while supported by the bearing assembly.

item_flows.name: Shaft rotation and alignment interaction
item_flows.notes: Shaft passes through inner race; shaft misalignment can cause bearing pivoting, and shaft rotation is accommodated by inner race rotation.

item_flows.name: Compression-ring bias force
item_flows.notes: Ring force holds the outer race against the retainer bearing seat; at this contact the compression ring offers less resistance to spherical motion than to rotational motion, preventing outer-race rotation while permitting self-alignment.

item_flows.name: Bearing spherical/pivot motion
item_flows.notes: Outer race and bearing pivot within retainer to align with shaft; an embodiment describes about 5-degree cone half-angle (claims 4–5).

requirements.statement: The bearing shall permit spherical movement of the outer race within the retainer to provide self-alignment with a shaft.
requirements.rationale: Claim 1; claims 4–5 describe about 5-degree alignment travel.

requirements.statement: The compression-ring interaction shall prevent rotational movement of the outer race as the inner race rotates in response to shaft rotation.
The retainer shall be press-installable in a receiving opening using a disclosed clinching or friction-fit embodiment.
requirements.rationale: Claims 6 and 9–11 disclose self-clinching and friction-fit alternatives.

actions.name: Align bearing and support shaft rotation

steps.description: Receive the shaft through the inner race.
Allow the bearing outer race to pivot within the retainer so the bearing axis aligns with the shaft, with the compression ring maintaining force against the bearing seat.
Permit the inner race to rotate with the shaft while the outer race remains rotationally restrained.
